plan_summary: Give the terminal failure-reason vocabulary a severity split in the two places the vocabulary actually lives: the reason sets in adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js (which decideLifecycle already scores) and the 'Failure-reason classes' section of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md (which the orchestrator reads). Three changes. (1) execution-report.js: add one NEW terminal reason, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, to NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS so a forged/unreadable evidence file halts non-retriably instead of scoring RETRY; add PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK to QUARANTINE_REASONS so the code finally computes the quarantine class phase-gates.md has documented for it since it was introduced; export a closed enum TERMINAL_FAILURE_REASONS plus failureReasonSeverity(reason) — a pure projection of the two existing sets, no second opinion — and tag the two FAIL branches that carry a distinct reason (consensus/blocking-dissent -> ADVOCATE_DISSENT, skills_clean/integrity -> EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH) with a structured gate-level failure_reason readable via a new terminalFailureReasonForGates(gates) helper, so an orchestrator sources the reason from a field instead of parsing gate detail prose. (2) phase-gates.md: replace the two-bullet 'Failure-reason classes' prose with a TABLE that defines every terminal reason and states its severity in the same row, adds the two new/clarified rows, and states the precedence rule that makes {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE the reason of last resort — a failing gate with a named reason NEVER flattens to the blanket reason. (3) artifact-layout.md: pin run_manifest.failure_reason as a closed enum sourced from that table (no free text) and rename the skill_trace breach class from 'the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT' to the new distinct reason. Deliberately NOT changed: the emitted execution_report.json/gates[] schema (so SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1.4.0 and the frozen parity harness, which pins '1.4.0' and lives in a blocked path, keeps passing), the CLI argument contract, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES and the exit codes.

file_change_proposal.description: The severity source. (a) Add 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' to NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS: today a job halted on a trace/output forgery or an unreadable evidence file has no reason of its own, so an orchestrator writes {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE and decideLifecycle scores RETRY — a severity downgrade on the one class that must never be retried. (b) Add 'PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK' to QUARANTINE_REASONS: phase-gates.md has listed it as quarantine-class since it was introduced while the code set omitted it, so a `failed` job halted on a second drift BLOCK scored RETRY; this aligns the code with its own long-documented meaning rather than redefining the reason (no fixture records it, so parity is unaffected). (c) Add a frozen TERMINAL_FAILURE_REASONS list (the closed enum, including the seven concrete {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE values) and failureReasonSeverity(reason) returning 'non-retriable' iff QUARANTINE_REASONS or NO_RETRY_REASONS contains it — exactly the test decideLifecycle already applies, so severity is a projection of the existing classification and can never disagree with the verdict. (d) Set a structured `failure_reason` on the two internal gate objects whose failure has a distinct terminal reason — evalConsensus's blocking-dissent FAIL (unresolved or operator-UPHELD) -> 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', evalSkillsClean's two integrity FAILs (unreadable/malformed evidence, trace-vs-validator mismatch) -> 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' — leaving every other FAIL branch null so a Critic fail and an ordinary skill failure keep routing to {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE unchanged. (e) Add terminalFailureReasonForGates(gates) returning { gate, failure_reason, severity } from the FIRST failing gate that carries one, reading only the `status` and `failure_reason` fields and never the `reason`/`detail` prose; return the internal gates array as a third key from buildReport and export the new helpers, so a programmatic orchestrator sources the reason+severity instead of re-deriving them. (f) Render the severity on the two reader surfaces that already print the reason — the markdown 'Failure reason:' line and the 'Failure reason recorded:' warning — via failureReasonSeverity. (g) Extend the header comment block with the rationale and an explicit note that the EMITTED report schema is unchanged, which is why SCHEMA_VERSION stays at 1.4.0. Do NOT touch DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, exitCodeFor, the gate key list, the CLI argument contract (parity/cli-contract pins one-argument usage and the exit-3 paths), or the shape of the emitted gates[] rows.

The vocabulary the orchestrator reads. Replace the two-bullet 'Failure-reason classes (port of phases.js reason sets)' section with a TABLE that defines every terminal reason and states its severity in the same row — columns: Terminal reason | Written when (gate/condition) | Terminal final_status | Halts immediately (ignores remaining budget) | Severity | Report verdict — covering CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, ADVOCATE_DISSENT, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (new), PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the seven enumerated {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE values so the enum stays CLOSED (no free-text reason). The ADVOCATE_DISSENT row must say the reason covers an unresolved dissent AND one the operator UPHELD, and the EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH row must name its two triggers (a skill_trace verdict that disagrees with its own validator stdout; an evidence file that exists and cannot be read/parsed). Keep the existing no-retry / quarantine-class bullets underneath as the two code sets so no reason's current meaning is lost, with PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED's 'no-retry but retriable verdict' note intact. Add two short rules under the table: (i) PRECEDENCE — {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE is the reason of last resort; when the failing gate matches a named row that row's reason is the terminal reason, so an upheld dissent terminates ADVOCATE_DISSENT and an integrity breach terminates EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, never REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE or TEST_GATE_FAILURE; (ii) SOURCING — the Severity column is the projection of the reason sets in scripts/execution-report.js and MUST be read from failureReasonSeverity()/terminalFailureReasonForGates(), never inferred from a gate's `detail` string, with a note that the attempt-only annotations ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED are deliberately absent from the table because they are never terminal. Update the Contents line 11 entry to match the new section title, and extend the Consensus rule 5 `uphold` bullet plus the 'Operator-directed repair' preamble to name the severity and point at the table.

The evidence contract. (a) In the run_manifest.json File-shapes prose (beside the existing `final_status` sentence at the end of the DEFINED-keys paragraph), state that `failure_reason` is null while running and, at terminal state, exactly one value of the CLOSED enum defined in the phase-gates.md failure-reason table — never free text, never an attempt-level annotation — and that its retriable/non-retriable severity is sourced from that table (which is itself the projection of the reason sets in scripts/execution-report.js), never re-derived from the report's gate `detail` strings. This is the rule the observed regression broke: a halt wrote a gate-detail sentence into the field. (b) In the skill_trace paragraph (the SC-8/F-55 block), replace 'an evidence-integrity breach, the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT' with the distinct new reason EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, stating it shares the non-retriable severity of MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT but is its own reason so a forged verdict is never reported as a missing artifact. (c) Add one sentence to append-only rule 5 (derived report files) noting that the report's `failure_reason` is echoed from run_manifest and that the terminal severity is a table lookup, not a re-derivation. Change nothing else: no new file shape, no new post-hoc field, no change to the rule-2 exhaustive list.

criteria_map.criterion: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
criteria_map.check_idea: Parse the new failure-reason table out of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md, collect the reason token and the Severity cell of every row, and assert: (1) the row set equals the exported TERMINAL_FAILURE_REASONS enum from adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js (both directions — no documented reason missing from the enum, no enum member missing a row); (2) every row's Severity cell is exactly failureReasonSeverity(reason); (3) severity appears as a COLUMN of the defining table, not as separate prose — assert each reason token and its severity word occur on the SAME table line. RED on the pre-change baseline (git archive main into scratch): the section is bullet prose with no table and no severity column, and the export does not exist.

criteria_map.criterion: An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Two assertions. Doc: the ADVOCATE_DISSENT table row names the UPHELD case (not just the unresolved one) and the precedence rule states that a gate failure matching a named row never records {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE — RED on baseline, where 'uphold' is described only in Consensus rule 5 and the blanket reason has no precedence rule. Code: build a synthetic job tree in the scratch root modelled on the existing quarantine_upheld_dissent shape (review/attempt_1/consensus/advocate.json carrying a dissent plus resolution.action 'uphold'), call buildReport(), and assert the returned internal gates array has the consensus gate at status 'fail' with failure_reason === 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', that terminalFailureReasonForGates() returns that reason with severity 'non-retriable', and that decideLifecycle({status:'failed', failureReason:'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', gates:[]}).decision === 'QUARANTINE'. RED on baseline: the gate object carries no failure_reason and the helper does not exist.

criteria_map.criterion: An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Three assertions. (1) decideLifecycle({status:'failed', failureReason:'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', gates:[]}).decision === 'QUARANTINE' and exitCodeFor(...) === 2 — RED on baseline, which returns RETRY/1 because the reason is in neither set; this is the severity downgrade the criterion names. (2) In a scratch job tree seeded with a trace/output mismatch (wrapper 'warn' over an output 'fail', the quarantine_trace_mismatch shape) and, separately, with an unreadable evidence file, buildReport()'s returned gates array has skills_clean at 'fail' with failure_reason === 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', while a tree whose only skills_clean failure is an ORDINARY validator fail leaves failure_reason null (so the blanket reason still applies where it should). (3) Both phase-gates.md (table row) and artifact-layout.md (skill_trace paragraph) name EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH as a distinct reason, and artifact-layout.md no longer describes the breach as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT's class without naming its own reason.

criteria_map.criterion: The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
criteria_map.check_idea: Totality plus a prose-immunity probe. Totality: for EVERY reason in the exported TERMINAL_FAILURE_REASONS, assert failureReasonSeverity(r) === (decideLifecycle({status:'failed', failureReason:r, gates:[]}).decision === 'QUARANTINE' ? 'non-retriable' : 'retriable') — this pins the severity function as a projection of the classification decideLifecycle already applies, so the two can never disagree. Prose-immunity: call terminalFailureReasonForGates on a hand-built gates array whose failing gate has a `reason`/`detail` string containing the words 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT' and 'EVIDENCE INTEGRITY' but whose structured failure_reason is null, and assert the helper returns null — a helper that read the prose would return a reason here. Doc: assert phase-gates.md carries the sourcing rule naming failureReasonSeverity()/terminalFailureReasonForGates() and forbidding derivation from gate detail text, and artifact-layout.md's run_manifest.failure_reason sentence says the same. Regression floor for the whole criterion set: node parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js stays 25/25 with identical decision, warn_flag and exit_code per fixture (contract constraint 4), and node parity/cli-contract/run-tests.js stays green.
